title: Synthetic traffic guardrails for heterogeneous inference zones
creator: Nadia Park
body:
Summary:
We need a robust subsystem for generating and applying synthetic traffic and guardrails during canary rollouts, A/B tests, and shadow deployments that span Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. The goal is to provide deterministic, tenant-aware exposure controls that respect environment-specific constraints (network egress, KMS access, rate limits, cost budgets) while enabling realistic failure and performance signals for automatic rollback decisions.

Background and motivation:
- Current rollout tooling relies on production traffic only and cannot reliably exercise tail latency, KV cache warm-up, and edge-case token patterns for models running on Dedicated or Private environments with different network/topology constraints.
- Without synthetic exercises, canaries may miss regressions that only appear under warm KV cache or under uncommon token distributions. This manifests as silent quality regressions or cost spikes post-promotion.
- We must avoid sending unfiltered synthetic data into customer-controlled Private zones or across egress restrictions. Synthetic traffic therefore needs environment-aware masks and a non-invasive execution path.

Scope and constraints:
- Works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments with a single control surface and environment-aware adapters.
- Must honor tenant isolation: synthetic traffic must be tagged and routed so it never mixes with customer data or leaves audited lanes.
- Enforce cost caps per canary run and per-tenant simulated traffic budget.
- Respect KMS/HSM policies in Private: synthetic requests should optionally use a signing shim instead of customer KMS keys.
- No change to existing public API contract; this is an orchestration/testing layer only.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Synthetic Traffic Engine (STE): a pluggable generator that can emit configurable request shapes (temperature, tokens, function calls, long-contexts, prefix sequences) and KV cache warm-up patterns. Runs as a separate runtime job in each environment and can optionally be scheduled to pre-warm Dedicated pools.
2) Environment Adapters: small adapters per mode: Hosted adapter (full synthetic), Dedicated adapter (respect node quotas and autoscaler hints), Private adapter (no external egress, use local signing shim, stricter rate limits).
3) Exposure Controller: horizon-based exposure controller that ramps synthetic + real traffic by tenant cohort. Supports combinatorial exposures: 5% real + 50 RPS synthetic for 1 hour, then 25% real + 100 RPS synthetic, etc. Each step has hard SLO/cost guardrails.
4) Safety Gate Engine: a lightweight decision engine that consumes telemetry (latency percentiles, error types, model divergence on golden prompts, cost burn rate) and computes a failure score per tenant and per rollout. Provides auto-rollback triggers with graded actions (throttle, revert portion of traffic, full rollback).
5) Telemetry and Golden-set evaluation: run structured golden prompts and parse structured output; compare divergence metrics and hallucination signals via our existing eval pipeline.

Telemetry and signals to capture:
- Tail latency (p99.9, p99.99) segmented by tenant and environment
- KV cache hit ratio during warm-up windows
- Model output divergence against golden prompts (BLEU/ROUGE-like and application-specific scoring)
- Error classes (OOM, RPC timeout, kernel failure) and their failure domains
- Cost burn delta vs baseline during synthetic runs
- Network/egress violations for Private adapter

Acceptance criteria (must all be met):
- STE can schedule and run synthetic traffic in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private adapters without leaking synthetic requests into production customer logs.
- Exposure Controller supports multi-stage ramp plans with per-stage cost caps and stops when caps are reached.
- Safety Gate Engine triggers rollback or throttle when a tenant-scoped failure score crosses configured thresholds and logs a clear reason.
- Rollout simulation harness can replay a planned ramp using historical traffic characteristics and predict two metrics: probability of rollback and estimated incremental cost. Prediction error <= 15% for cost and <= 10% for rollback probability on sampled historical runs.
- End-to-end documentation and runbook updated with preflight checklist and postmortem guidance.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Prototype STE + Hosted adapter; basic golden-set runner and telemetry. Create canary plan schema extensions for synthetic stages.
- Week 2: Build Exposure Controller and Safety Gate Engine; integrate with Hosted rollout UI for visualization.
- Week 3: Add Dedicated adapter with autoscaler hints and cost-cap enforcement; run internal Dedicated canary for a non-customer model.
- Week 4: Add Private adapter constraints (no egress, signing shim); run controlled synthetic exercise with SE partner.
- Week 5: Stability, simulations, and instrumentation; ship runtime-1.22 feature flag behind org opt-in.

Risk analysis and mitigations:
- Risk: Synthetic traffic accidentally counted as customer usage. Mitigation: tag all synthetic requests with immutable header and route through an internal meter that is excluded from billing; add billing audit tests.
- Risk: KMS access in Private. Mitigation: use signing shim and keep synthetic keys local; run security review.
- Risk: Cost overruns from synthetic runs. Mitigation: hard budget caps and automated stop at 80% of cap.

Next steps / tickets to create:
- ENG-58378: STE hosted prototype PR and golden sets
- ENG-58380: Exposure Controller UI + API schema
- ENG-58381: Dedicated adapter + autoscaler hints
- ENG-58382: Private adapter signing shim and egress guard

- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Synthetic+Traffic+Guardrails (draft)
- Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/186
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1423
- Internal dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/synthetic-canary-overview

If blocked: contact Ravi Menon for Dedicated infra quotas and Nadia Park for test/golden prompt curation.
acceptance_criteria: STE runs in all three environment adapters and is opt-in per org
Per-stage cost caps enforced and expose stop reason in rollout UI
Safety Gate Engine provides tenant-scoped rollback with clear audit logs
Simulation harness predicts rollback probability and cost within tolerances
comments: 2025-02-16 - Nadia Park: Initial spike complete. STE can emit sequences that exercise KV warm-up. Captured initial p99 delta in Hosted.
2025-02-18 - Ravi Menon: Hooked Exposure Controller to rollout API. Need autoscaler hints from Dedicated infra team (blocking: infra-req-12).
2025-02-20 - Security (Isha Kaur): Private adapter must not use org KMS keys for synthetic runs; required signing shim noted.
2025-02-22 - Eng Review (Marco Li): Suggested adding tenant heatmap in UI to visualize which tenants are affected by synthetic ramps.
2025-02-24 - QA (Lina Gomez): Ran simulation against last 10 canaries; false-positive rollback rate acceptable but need more golden prompts for long-context cases.
notes: This ticket emphasizes safety-first rollout automation. Keep the default off for orgs and require opt-in with clear billing visibility. Coordinate with SEs before Private runs.
